chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan informed me, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Abū Ḥabīb al-Asadī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام.
He said: I heard him say, concerning a man who has a nosebleed while he is in a state of wudu (ablution), he said: "He washes away the traces of the blood and performs salat (prayer)."

key_terms.آثَارَ الدَّمِ: the traces of blood remaining on the body

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he gets a nosebleed while in a state of wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person who experiences a nosebleed while in a state of wudu (ablution). It indicates that he should wash away the blood's traces and then perform salat (prayer), showing that the occurrence described does not itself necessitate renewing wudu in this report.
